title: Jenna Johnson Dances With a Broken Nose During ‘DWTS’ Grammy Night
summary: Jenna Johnson *nose* the show must go on, even after a brutal injury.
story: Jenna Johnson *nose* the show must go on, even after a brutal injury.
The “Dancing With the Stars” pro shared that she suffered a broken nose ahead of the Nov. 10 Grammy Night episode.

“Alright, you guys. So, last night I definitely broke my nose during camera blocking,” Johnson said in an Instagram video. “If you can see this right side, right here and right here, a little swollen.”
“No black eyes today, which is awesome. But if my nose looks four times its size, that’s why,” she added with a thumbs up.
Johnson, who is partnered with actor Harry Shum Jr. captioned her video: “Salsa: 1, Jenna’s Nose: 0. Happy Show Day.”
Fellow pros hyped her up and sent well wishes, including Emma Slater who wrote, “You’re a beast. Like seriously.”
Dylan Efron, who competed last season, added, “Don’t need noses to dance 💪crush it tonight!”
Her partner Shum Jr. also commented, “WHO DID THIS TO YOU?? ….oh…sorry…BUT YOU ARE A TOTAL BADASS!!!!”
Johnson’s husband and fellow pro Valentin Chmerkovskiy added, “1of1 ❤️ still a baddie.”
During the “DWTS” episode, co-host Julianne Hough asked Johnson how she was feeling after her injury.
“I did break my nose but I feel amazing. I’m so happy that I get to dance,” she said, as Shum Jr. apologized to her.
“It’s OK,” she replied. “Salsa elbow, it’s fine.”
The couple didn’t have anything to worry about after the judges gave them a 29 out of 30 for their salsa routine to “Die with A Smile” by Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars.
With only three episodes left of Season 30 of “DWTS,” the stakes are high. Johnson and Shum Jr., however, continue to be at the top of the leaderboard, as are Chmerkovskiy and Jenna Dewan.
When speaking to TODAY.com in October, the husband and wife shared that there is no competition between them.

“I’ve never been competitive with Jenna. I’m only passionate about creating, only passionate about my art or my work or the effort that I put into ‘Dancing With the Stars,’” Chmerkovskiy said. “So, it’s not a competition of, can I do it better than her? The competition is, can I produce my best work? And I think both of us can do that. I could support her and be ‘competitive’ at the same time.”

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes Announce They’re Expecting Baby No. 4
summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes are adding another bundle of joy to their family.
story: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes are adding another bundle of joy to their family.
The 31-year-old Kansas City Chiefs quarterback and wife announced that they are expecting their fourth child together.
“Another blessing from God & then there were 6,” reads the caption on their joint Nov. 10 Instagram post.
The couple shared photos of the two of them with their three children — daughter Sterling, 5, son Patrick “Bronze,” 3, and 19-month daughter Golden Raye — at the beach in color-coordinated looks.
The photos are sweet and one shows the NFL star touching his wife’s belly, while the last photo in the slideshow has all of them cradling her bump.
Their friends, family and followers congratulated them in the comments section. Patrick Mahomes’ mom, Randi Mahomes, wrote, “I cannot wait!! Congratulations love yall.”
“OH MY GOSH!! Congratulations!!!” one person wrote, while another added, “Eeeekkk!! One loved little babe already!! Congrats guys!”
One follower also suggested names for their baby on the way, “Omg if it’s a boy COPPER, and a girl SILVER. I’m betting on it early.”
The high school sweethearts welcomed their first child, Sterling, in February 2021. They then got married in 2022.
After welcoming Golden, Patrick Mahomes predicted that they wouldn’t continue to expand their family.
“I’m done, I’ll say that. No. 3 — I said three, and I’m done,” he said at the time with a smile. “No, it’s awesome. I always wanted to have kids young. I got to grow up in the locker room.”

However, it appears he changed his mind. Since then, Brittany Mahomes has continued to share sweet family moments on her Instagram story, most recently of her and their kids “making memories they will never forget” at Chiefs’ games and dressing up for Halloween.

title: Dustin Hoffman Says ‘Tootsie’ Made Him See ‘Women in a New Way’
summary: Actor Dustin Hoffman reveals how playing Dorothy Michaels in “Tootsie” made him realize that if he actually was a woman, he would have never gotten the job.
story: Legendary actor Dustin Hoffman has a long list of award-winning movies including “All the President’s Men,” “The Graduate,” “Kramer vs. Kramer” and, of course, “Tootsie.”
The 1982 film stars Hoffman as Michael Dorsey, an out-of-work actor wins a part on a soap opera by auditioning as a woman.

In his new memoir, “Look At Me,” Hoffman writes that the movie title comes from his mother, who called him “My little Tootsie Wootsie” and that the genesis for the film came while he was ribbing a close friend about coming to terms “with his feminine side.”
“The idea that every man has a feminine side and every woman has a masculine side was something I’d been thinking about a lot while I was making ‘Kramer,’” Hoffman says in the book.
Though it began as a joke, the idea stuck with Hoffman, who continued to mull it over with longtime wife, Lisa, and screenwriter Murray Schisgal.
“There’s something to this,” he says of their conversations in the book. “There’s something about coming to terms with the woman inside you that’s really interesting.”
It made the actor reflect on how things might have been different if he’d been born a female and writes that the idea eventually became the screenplay for the Oscar-winning movie “Tootsie.”
Once the movie took shape, Hoffman began doing research to play Dorothy Michaels, his feminine alter ego in “Tootsie,” and in many ways it changed his life.

“Dorothy Michaels made me see women in a new way,” he writes in the memoir. According to the actor, it took him more than a year and a half to get to the point where “I could go out on the street as her and nobody looked twice.”

Though he’d accomplished what he set out to do, Hoffman says in the book that he was “upset” that while he could easily pass as Dorothy, no amount of makeup and prosthetics were ever going to make him “beautiful” by society’s “narrow definition” of beauty.
It led to an epiphany.
“When I was young, I told my aunt Pearl I wanted to an actor. She looked genuinely puzzled when she replied, ‘You? You’re too homely!’” he says in the memoir.

He says his aunt Pearl’s judgment would later ring out on the cover of Life Magazine, which “once published the sentence ‘If Dustin Hoffman’s face was his fortune, he’d have been condemned to a life of poverty.’”
And, after the release of “The Graduate,” Hoffman writes that “critics seemed almost offended that someone as ugly as me got to be in a movie.”
But the deeper realization, according to Hoffman, was that despite being ridiculed for his appearance, he was still getting work.
“I got insulted plenty for my looks when I started starring in movies. But if I’d been a woman, I never would have been cast in the first place.”
His understanding of that double standard crystallized during the filming of “Tootsie.”

“Before I played Dorothy Michaels,” he writes, “I hadn’t considered the endless, tedious, expensive demands put on women to be ‘feminine.’ Wearing heels and a bra and stockings, having to spend hours putting on makeup and shaving my legs - and then getting rashes shaving my legs - by the end of ‘Tootsie,’ I thought, ‘F--- this.’”
But more than the time and money, Hoffman writes that it was a matter of dignity.

“There is something really demoralizing about performing these neverending rituals that suggest, ‘I am no good as I am. My face my hair, my body are wrong, and require covering up, altering, apologizing for.”
Hoffman went on to earn an Academy Award nomination for the movie, which also stars Jessica Lange, Teri Garr, Bill Murray, Geena Davis, Dabney Coleman and Charles Durning.
Looking back on the film, Hoffman writes, “‘Tootsie’ has been a great part of my life.”

title: Jamie Lee Curtis on Being ‘Lost’ as a Teen and the One Person Who Noticed
summary: Jamie Lee Curtis reveals the educator who saw her “as a human” when she was in school and how she paid tribute to him in her latest series “Newlyweds.”
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com spotlights the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.

Jamie Lee Curtis is marking nearly 50 years in film and television. But if you think that means she’s winding down, think again. Curtis, who celebrates her 68th birthday later this month, is busier than ever and loving every minute.
“I am a creative person. I’ve been a creative person since I was, really, born,” she tells TODAY.com. “But I became an actor when I was 18, and I have never been in charge.
Until now, that is.

Curtis launched her very first sitcom, “Newlyweds,” on Oct. 23. The charming NBC comedy stars real-life husband and wife Tim Daly and Téa Leoni as James and Jeanie, a 60ish couple who meet on a blind date, then marry on a whim soon after.

The premise is not unlike Curtis’ own marriage to actor and filmmaker Christopher Guest. The pair, who’ve been together for over 40 years, met after Curtis saw Guest’s photo in a magazine and told a friend, “I’m going to marry that guy.”

Though she gave her phone number to Guest’s agent, she never heard back. However, a chance meeting at a restaurant a couple months later led to a date. Then another. Four months after that, they tied the knot in 1984.

“I got married to a guy I had never spent more than 72 hours with at one time. We got married within four months of meeting, so our union was really fast. So, clearly the concept of the show came from my own personal life,” the Oscar winner says.
While Curtis’ and Guest’s whirlwind romance may play a part in “Newlyweds,” Curtis says the true inspiration for the series lies in a limo ride and its driver.

Curtis explained that during a 2019 trip to New York, she was chatting with the driver of her car, a man in his 60s, and was thunderstruck after he talked about his divorce and mentioned his “new wife.”
“And I went (gasps), ‘My new wife?’ That’s a sitcom about people in their 60s, who go on a blind date and hook up!” she said of the a-ha moment.
She fleshed out the idea with creative partner Gail Lerner (who has since left the show), and together they developed “Newlyweds.”
Curtis not only serves as executive producer on the series, but she also has a recurring role as Claudia, Daly’s overbearing ex-wife.
“I’m not at all like her. I’m not disruptive and she is disruptive on purpose,” Curtis says of her character. “I like to refer to her as the ‘shaker of the snow globe.’”
More Than Just a Name
While Curtis doesn’t have much in common with Claudia, she does share a special connection with her character’s last name.
Prior to the launch of the show, Curtis says she was asked to give her character a surname and didn’t hesitate.
“I said, ‘I want her to be named after my eighth grade American history teacher, George Fourges, because he was the only teacher in my life who ever saw me as a human. Ever,” Curtis says.
“I went through school, barely, and no one saw me. I could not do anything. I’m a functional illiterate. The delivery system of education did not work for me,” she says.
“I was lost, and no one noticed except George Fourges and so I named Claudia as an honor to George Fourges,” Curtis says. “We always remember our one and only teacher.”
She also shares a special message for other “one-and-only teachers”: “God bless you, God bless you. Because without you, people really, really, really struggle, and what you do is gorgeous.”
‘Everything Brings Me Joy’
According to Curtis, this latest chapter in her career is a fulfilling one. But, the actor explains, just about everything for her is fulfilling these days.
“Everything brings me joy. Everything, I mean everything,” explains Curtis. “Just being alive brings me joy.”
The reason, in part, is because she’s keenly aware of how fleeting it all is and wants to take advantage of every minute she can.
“I’m just old enough to know long this lasts and it doesn’t last that long. So, I’m trying to sort of cram a lot into a short amount of time.”

She says she also gets joy from the fact that “Newlyweds” airs on network television, every Friday in NBC’s 8:30 p.m. ET slot. Curtis says it allows people to get together and watch a TV show like they used to do in years past.

“What we’re offering in between the advertising is something beautiful. This is aspirational, it’s relatable, it’s funny, it’s poignant, it’s silly, it’s a little exaggerated. It’s a little sexy,” she says. “It’s just life kind of being brought to you, which is the history of sitcoms, right?”
More than that, Curtis hopes her return to the traditional sitcom will inspire others to do the same.

“If at 68 years old, I have a hand in bringing sitcoms back to an art form where other networks start going, ‘Ooh, let’s copy NBC and put some sitcoms on,’ I will feel incredibly gratified,” she says.

title: Why Dustin Hoffman Almost Quit ‘Rain Man’
summary: Dustin Hoffman wrote in his new memoir that he almost quit Rain Man. Here’s why.
story: One of Dustin Hoffman’s most memorable roles is his portrayal of Ray Babbitt in the 1988 movie “Rain Man.”

Playing a savant opposite Tom Cruise, the role earned Hoffman the second best actor Academy Award of his career (the first was for “Kramer vs. Kramer”) and shed new light and understanding on neurodiversity.
However, according to Hoffman, it’s a role that almost didn’t happen.
In his new memoir, “Look At Me,” the 90-year-old reveals that after watching himself as Ray Babbitt in the unedited footage of the movie, he “almost quit.”

“I couldn’t find the character,” Hoffman writes in the memoir, saying that as he watched the dailies of his performance with director Barry Levinson, he felt “ridiculous,” “totally fake” and thought to himself, “This is awful, I’ve got to get out of this.”
But it was Levinson’s calm reassurance that kept the veteran actor from walking away.
“‘Give it a couple weeks,’ he told me. ‘If you still can’t get him, quit then. Just see if you can find one moment that feels authentic,’” Hoffman writes in “Look At Me” of Levinson’s advice.

Hoffman agreed to keep trying and in a pivotal scene with Cruise, he improvised, something Hoffman says is “one of my favorite ways to work.” Except it didn’t work — or at least Hoffman didn’t think it did.

“It did not go well,” he writes. “Tom (Cruise) was inhabiting Charlie Babbitt, improvising wonderfully, asking me questions: ‘Do you understand, Ray? You got that, Ray?’ But I was stumped. So I just kept saying, ‘Yeah. Yeah.’”

When they finished, Hoffman writes that he was “depressed” and it furthered his conviction that he simply wasn’t right for the role and even apologized to Levinson for messing up the scene. But the director had seen something in the footage that Hoffman hadn’t.
“He showed me the improvised part of the playback, and when I was saying ‘Yeah. Yeah’ ... that was it,” writes Hoffman.

“That was the guy. Overwhelmed, intensely focused, unsure of himself, and trying so hard to do what was expected of him, without really understanding what that was. That was me during the improvisation, and that was Ray most of the time he was around other people,” he writes in “Look At Me.”

It was a revelation for the actor, who writes that having a director like Levinson allowed him to see what he couldn’t. “I didn’t think I was playing Ray when I was saying, ‘Yeah. Yeah.’ I had inadvertently found him in myself.”
The movie went on to earn four Oscars, including Hoffman’s best actor award, best picture, best director and best original screenplay.

title: Carson Daly Gets Standing Ovation From ‘The Voice’ Coaches After Kelly Clarkson Congratulates Him on Saturday TODAY Gig
summary: Carson Daly was surprised with a standing ovation during the Nov. 9 episode of “The Voice” after Kelly Clarkson congratulated him on his Saturday TODAY job.
story: Carson Daly was surprised with a standing ovation during the Nov. 9 episode of “The Voice.”

As the host kicked off the first live show, Kelly Clarkson took a moment to congratulate him for one of his latest career accomplishments. After the Top 13 performed to a Backstreet Boys song and Carson teased what was to come during the episode, Kelly raised her hand to get his attention.
“Question from the audience,” Carson joked, as Kelly said, “Carson, I wanted to say congratulations on Saturday TODAY. You’re the new anchor.”
As Carson thanked her, the rest of the coaches, Adam Levine, Riley Green and Queen Latifah, got on their feet and clapped, as did the audience.
“I am an anchorman now, a trusted source of news,” Carson said, before starting the competition. “Alright, let’s start the performances.”

Carson has been a television staple for years since his early “Total Request Live” days, followed by his stint on late-night with “Last Call with Carson Daly.” Already an integral part of TODAY, he made his debut as the permanent co-anchor of Saturday TODAY alongside Laura Jarrett on Nov. 7.
Ahead of the Nov. 9 “The Voice” episode, Adam recalled the first time meeting Carson and shared how much he appreciated his support over the years.

“I think it was on ‘Last Call with Carson Daly’ back in the day. He was one of the first guys to ever put us on TV. And I am always thankful, and I thank him all the time,” he told TODAY. “Thank you for putting me on TV. Appreciate you.”
Adam, along with Kelly, Riley and Blake Shelton, had previously sent surprise messages to Carson to celebrate his first official day on the job.

“Maybe since it’s the weekend show, to be more entertainment, not as much breaking news, which is good for you because I don’t think people take you that serious anyway,” quipped Blake, whose 2021 wedding to Gwen Stefani was officiated by Carson. “Anyway, buddy, good luck, love you, and congratulations.”

title: ‘The Voice’ Live Shows Kick Off With Backstreet Boys-Inspired Performance, America’s Save Winner and Elimination
summary: The live shows are officially kicking off on “The Voice.” Find out who is remaining on each team.
story: The live shows have officially kicked off on “The Voice.”
Part one of the Y2K live shows took place on Nov. 9, with the sensational talent singing songs from the late ‘90s and early 2000s.
The show opened with host Carson Daly standing outside the set of “The Voice” with a crowd holding up “Total Request Live”-inspired posters.
“And this is really taking me back to Times Square, 1999,” Carson said, before sharing how the Top 13 would be singing a song that “swept the swept the global charts and defined the late ‘90s.”

The singers competing then appeared on the stage all decked out in white as they sang “Everybody (Backstreet’s Back)” by Backstreet Boys. It also included the reveal of Kyle Davis as the singer who America saved.

Last episode, dubbed Cut Week, saw coaches Riley Green, Adam Levine, Queen Latifah and Kelly Clarkson dramatically trim their teams down to three singers each. Those artists will continue to compete against one other during the next six live shows.
Singers from Team Queen and Team Adam would only be singing during the Nov. 9 episode, with Team Kelly and Team Riley next week.

Prior to the first live show, Green told TODAY.com that he’s had time to work with his artists “and help build them up some confidence to get ready for these lives because that’s gonna be tough. It’s nerve-wrecking to have to perform live on television for an audience and (it) be the biggest audience a lot of them ever performed for.”
He added that his strategy is “find the things I think they do the best and to highlight those.”
Levine also told TODAY.com he’s such a fan of his team “and I am proud of them regardless of how far everybody gets.”

“I told them this the other day, focus on the task at hand, focus on every night. It’s a win to be on the show,” he added. “Every moment you get to be on the show is a victory to me because you never know if you’re gonna win, but just let the victory come unknowingly.”
Additionally, Clarkson also expressed her excitement for the live shows.

“This is bringing humanity to the table,” she told TODAY.com. “Sometimes we lose a little bit of that in a lot of industries. I think that’s why people really tune in for these live events because they feel like they’re there with us. They feel like it’s happening with them, and there’s something organic and beautiful about that.”

This year, “The Voice” is also incorporating different themes for their live shows. The Nov. 9 and Nov. 16 episodes will be Y2K Night, followed by Dolly Parton Night on Nov. 23 and TikTok Night on Nov. 30.
